8: # SEO Content: Content Strategy
9: 
10: Guides content strategy for SEO: topic clusters, pillar pages, cluster articles, and editorial planning. For content marketing across all channels (blog, email, social, video), see **content-marketing**. For translation workflow and multilingual content, see **translation**.
11: 
12: **When invoking**: On **first use**, if helpful, open with 1-2 sentences on what this skill covers and why it matters, then provide the main output. On **subsequent use** or when the user asks to skip, go directly to the main output.
13: 
14: ## Initial Assessment
15: 
16: **Check for project context first:** If `.claude/project-context.md` or `.cursor/project-context.md` exists, read it for product, audience, and proof points.
17: 
18: Identify:
19: 1. **Keywords**: From keyword research — see **keyword-research** for discovery and clustering
20: 2. **Existing content**: What already exists
21: 3. **Resources**: Content capacity, tools
22: 4. **Goals**: Traffic, conversions, authority
23: 
24: **Product-Led SEO**: Do SEO around product/users, not around industry/search engines. See **seo-strategy** for Product-Led SEO principle, products suited for SEO, and workflow order.
25: 
26: ## Topic Clusters
27: 
28: Topic clusters organize content by **topic** rather than isolated keywords. A **pillar page** covers a broad core topic; **cluster articles** cover subtopics; all connect via internal links. This signals topical authority to search engines and AI systems.
29: 
30: ### Structure
31: 
32: ```
33: Pillar page (broad topic, 2,000-5,000+ words)
34:     <-> internal links
35: Cluster 1 (subtopic, 800-2,500 words)
36: Cluster 2 (subtopic)
37: ...
38: Cluster 6-12 (subtopics)
39:     <-> cluster to cluster links
40: ```
41: 
42: ### Pillar Page
43: 
44: | Attribute | Guideline |
45: |-----------|-----------|
46: | **Length** | 2,000-5,000+ words; comprehensive guide |
47: | **Keyword** | Broad head term with search volume |
48: | **Role** | Hub; links to all cluster articles; targets primary topic |
49: | **Conversion** | Link to product/feature pages where relevant |
50: 
51: ### Cluster Articles
52: 
53: | Attribute | Guideline |
54: |-----------|-----------|
55: | **Count** | 6-12 articles per pillar (minimum 6 for authority) |
56: | **Length** | 800-2,500 words each; focused on one subtopic |
57: | **Keyword** | Long-tail, specific intent per article |
58: | **Links** | Each cluster links to pillar; pillar links back; related clusters link to each other |
59: 
60: ### Internal Linking Model
61: 
62: | Link type | Purpose |
63: |-----------|---------|
64: | **Pillar to Cluster** | Hub distributes authority; users discover subtopics |
65: | **Cluster to Pillar** | Signals relationship; passes equity to hub |
66: | **Cluster to Cluster** | Related subtopics; strengthens topical coverage |
67: 
68: ### Structure and Content Equally Important
69: 
70: **Framework and body quality both matter**: TOC, chapter logic, and content depth are all essential for SEO and UX. Weak structure undermines strong writing; weak writing undermines strong structure. Plan both from the start.
71: 
72: ### Why Topic Clusters Work
73: 
74: - **Topical authority**: Rank for multiple variations; comprehensive coverage signals expertise
75: - **Avoid cannibalization**: One page per topic/keyword; no competing pages
76: - **Better internal linking**: Clear logic; crawlers understand structure
77: - **AI citations**: Clustered content gets ~42% more AI citations than standalone
78: - **Traffic**: ~30% more organic traffic; rankings hold ~2.5x longer
79: 
80: ### Implementation Steps
81: 
82: 1. **Choose 3-7 core topics** -> business relevance, search demand, competitive opportunity
83: 2. **Map subtopics** -> People Also Ask, competitor analysis, keyword tools
84: 3. **Content audit** -> Identify existing pages that can become pillar or cluster; find gaps
85: 4. **Build clusters first** (optional) -> Cluster pages often rank first; add pillar after
86: 5. **Create pillar** -> Comprehensive guide; link to all clusters
87: 6. **Establish links** -> Pillar <-> cluster; cluster <-> cluster
88: 7. **Update quarterly** -> Maintain freshness and authority
89: 
90: ### Example
91: 
92: - **Pillar**: "SEO Guide" (targets "SEO")
93: - **Clusters**: "Technical SEO," "On-Page SEO," "Link Building," "Content SEO," "Local SEO," "E-E-A-T"
94: 
95: ## Content Types
96: 
97: | Type | Use | SEO Fit |
98: |------|-----|---------|
99: | **How-to guides** | Informational intent; high share potential | High -> matches search intent |
100: | **Comparisons** | Commercial intent; "X vs Y" | High |
101: | **List posts** | "Top 10," "Best X" | High |
102: | **Glossaries** | Definition queries; internal link hub | High |
103: | **Tools/calculators** | Linkable assets; engagement | High |
104: | **Case studies** | Proof; conversion support | Medium -> supports conversion |
105: | **Funding / PR** | Funding rounds, acquisitions | Low -> brand/PR, not search-driven |
106: | **Product updates** | Feature launches, release notes | Low -> internal audience |
107: | **News / Trending** | Industry news, hot topics | Medium -> quick spikes, short shelf life |
108: 
109: ### Evergreen vs Timely Content Mix
110: 
111: - **Evergreen** (70-75%): Pillar guides, how-tos, comparisons, glossaries. Drives long-term traffic, backlinks, authority. Refresh every 6-12 months.
112: - **Timely** (25-30%): Seasonal, trending, news. Generates quick traffic, shows topical relevance. Link timely pieces into evergreen pillars.
113: - **Balance**: Too much evergreen = blog feels stale; too much timely = irregular traffic, constant content churn.
114: 
115: ## Editorial Calendar
116: 
117: - Map keywords to content pieces
118: - Prioritize by opportunity (volume -> intent -> feasibility)
119: - Schedule by capacity
120: - Include update schedule for existing content
121: 
122: ## Output Format
123: 
124: - **Topic cluster** map (pillar + 6-12 clusters)
125: - **Content calendar** (topics, keywords, deadlines)
126: - **Internal linking** plan
127: - **Update plan** for existing content
128: 
129: ## Related Skills
130: 
131: - **content-marketing**: Content types, formats, channels, repurposing; SEO content is one channel
132: - **translation**: Multilingual content; translation workflow, glossary; avoid thin translations
133: - **seo-strategy**: SEO workflow order, Product-Led SEO, audit approach; use when planning SEO from scratch
134: - **website-structure**: Plan which pages to build; structure informs content clusters and pillar placement
135: - **keyword-research**: Keywords drive content plan
136: - **programmatic-seo**: Programmatic SEO for scaling pages with template + data; complements topic clusters
137: - **content-optimization**: Word count, H2 keywords, keyword density, multimedia, lists -> on-page content optimization
138: - **internal-links**: Clusters need internal linking
139: - **link-building**: Content strategy creates linkable assets
140: - **heading-structure**: Content structure uses headings"}}
